method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the three comparisons and four partial-function regions, with exact formula and macro parity after one bounded documented source correction. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Russell self-membership, the all-functions analogue, computability diagonalization, and the total/partial versus computable/noncomputable classification exercise.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For S={x:x notin x}, self-membership yields S in S iff S notin S, so no such set exists and a set of all sets conflicts with set-theory axioms.
samples.checks: OLCMP-016 corrects the frozen undefined capital X to S. The paradox is kept distinct from the asserted contradiction and the set-existence conclusion.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An alleged F from all functions to {0,1}, defined by whether f belongs to its own domain and yields zero, would make F(F)=0 iff F(F)=1, so it is not a function on that putative domain. For an enumeration of partial computable f_x, a total G returning one when f_x(x) halts at zero is a set-theoretic function but cannot be computable, since G=f_k would yield G(k)=1 iff G(k)=0.
samples.checks: The two distinct conclusions, conditional test in each case formula, total type of G, and absence of a set-theoretic paradox in the third case are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Partial N-to-N functions occupy four regions according to totality and partial computability: total computable, partial computable but not total, total not computable, and neither. The reader is asked to draw two overlapping regions and give an example in each.
samples.checks: The four categories, default use of function for total functions, overlapping-region exercise and all displayed N symbols remain.
